summary: 番茄从安第斯地区的小果实变成形状、大小各异的作物，长期选育也缩窄了遗传多样性。育种者尝试把抗病等性状引回栽培种，同时保留传统品种受欢迎的风味。
logic: 传统番茄引出起源问题
果实大小与形状的选择

paragraphs.brief: 以他们的品味、颜色和有机外观而闻名的传承的西红柿是园丁和当地种植食品的倡导者们最喜爱的。
sentences: Famous for their taste, color, and organic appearance, heirloom tomatoes are favorites of gardeners and advocates of locally grown foods.
以他们的品味、颜色和有机外观而闻名的传承的西红柿是园丁和当地种植食品的倡导者们最喜爱的。

The tomato enthusiast might conclude that, given the immense varieties, heirlooms must have a more diverse and superior set of genes than the tomatoes available in grocery stores, those ordinary hybrid varieties such as cherry and plum.
番茄爱好者可能得出结论，鉴于品种繁多，传家宝必须拥有比杂货店的西红柿(樱桃和李子等普通混合品种)更多样化和更好的基因组。

However, their seeming diversity is only skin-deep: heirlooms are actually feeble and inbred—the defective product of breeding experiments that began hundreds of years ago, and exploded thanks to enthusiastic backyard gardeners.
然而，它们看起来的多样化只是皮肤深处：传承的宝物实际上是微弱的，是数百年前开始的育种实验的缺陷产物，并且由于热情的后院园艺人而爆炸。
“The irony of all this,” says Steven Tanksley, a geneticist at Cornell University, “is that all that diversity of heirlooms can be accounted for by a handful of genes.
康奈尔大学的遗传学家史蒂文·坦斯利(Steven Tanksley)说，“所有这一切的讽刺之处在于，所有传承宝藏的多样性都可以由少数基因来解释。
There are probably no more than 10 mutant genes that create the diversity of heirlooms you see.”
可能没有超过10个变种基因来创造你看到的传世宝的多样性

But rather than simply proving that the myth about the heirlooms’ diversity is wrong, Tanksley’s deconstruction of the tomato genome, along with work by others, is showing how a small berry-like fruit from the Andes became one of the world’s top crops.
但坦斯利不仅不能证明关于传世宝多样性的神话是错误的，而且要说明安第斯山脉的微小果实如何成为世界顶级作物之一。

paragraphs.brief: 种植的番茄是阴暗家庭的成员，其中包括新世界的作物，如马铃薯，在15世纪克里斯托弗·哥伦布把他们带回西班牙之后，这些作物遍及全球。
sentences: The cultivated tomato is a member of the nightshade family that includes New World crops such as the potato, which spread around the globe after Christopher Columbus brought them back to Spain in the 15th century.
种植的番茄是阴暗家庭的成员，其中包括新世界的作物，如马铃薯，在15世纪克里斯托弗·哥伦布把他们带回西班牙之后，这些作物遍及全球。
But whereas scientists have uncovered a wealth of archaeological evidence on early farming practices in the New World, the record is blank when it comes to the tomato.
但是科学家们发现了大量关于新世界早期耕作方法的考古证据，而在番茄方面，记录是空白的。
The modern tomato seems to have its origins in the Andes in South America and may have been domesticated in Veracruz, Mexico.
现代番茄似乎起源于南美洲的安第斯山脉，可能已在墨西哥维拉克鲁斯被驯化。
Primitive varieties still grow throughout the Americas.
原始品种仍在整个美洲生长。
All told, botanists call as many as 13 species “tomatoes” and consider an additional four to be closely related.
植物学家称13种种类型为"番茄"，另外还有4种类型被认为是密切相关的。

paragraphs.brief: 人们可能会认为，这些已知的野生物种之一已成为今天的作物，但情况并非如此：母番茄从未被发现。
sentences: One might assume that one of these known wild species became today’s cultivated crop, but that’s not the case: the Mother Tomato has never been found.
人们可能会认为，这些已知的野生物种之一已成为今天的作物，但情况并非如此：母番茄从未被发现。
The closest relative is the currant tomato, which, based on genetic comparisons, split from today’s tomato some 1.4 million years ago.
最接近的是卷曲番茄，根据基因比较，它与大约140万年前的今天的番茄分开。
So researchers like Tanksley have to work backward, crossing tomato varieties and species in order to understand how various genes influence shape and size.
因此，像Tanksley这样的研究人员必须落后地工作，跨越番茄品种和物种，以便了解各种基因如何影响形状和大小。
Once isolated, Tanksley later inserts those genes into other tomato varieties to make his case with a dramatic transformation.
一旦被孤立，Tanksley 稍后把这些基因插入到其他番茄品种中使他的情况发生巨变。

paragraphs.brief: 除了大小，番茄种植者也选择形状。
sentences: Tanksley concludes from his analyses that in their effort to make bigger, tastier, and faster-growing fruit, our ancestors ultimately exploited just 30 mutations out of the tomato’s 35,000 genes.
Tanksley从他的分析中得出结论，在他们努力制造更大的，美味的，和更快生长的水果，我们的祖先最终只剥削了番茄的35,000个基因中的30个突变。
Most of these genes have only small effects on tomato size and shape, but recently Tanksley and his colleagues reported that they found a gene that increases fruit size by 50 percent.
这些基因大多对番茄大小和形状的影响很小，但最近Tanksley和他的同事报告说，他们发现了一个将水果大小增加50%的基因。
It was probably the most important event in domestication.
这可能是家庭化最重要的事件。

The first written record of tomatoes—from Spain in the 1500s—confirms that this mutation, which enlarges tomatoes by producing compartments known as locules, existed back in the same yellow tomatoes that gave Italians the word pomodoro, or golden apple.
1500年代来自西班牙的第一份西红柿书面记录证实，这种通过产出称为小木薯的隔间而扩大西红柿的突变，存在于给意大利人以pomodoro这个词或金苹果的同一黄西红柿中。
Besides size, tomato farmers also selected for shape.
除了大小，番茄种植者也选择形状。
To discover those genes, Esther van der Knaap, a Tanksley alumna now at The Ohio State University, took a gene from one heirloom tomato and inserted it into a wild relative.
为了发现这些基因 Esther van der Knaap，Tanksley 校友，现在在俄亥俄州立大学，从一个传世的番茄中提取了一个基因，并插入了一个野生亲戚。
She observed that, as a result, the tiny fruits became shaped like pears.
她注意到，因此，这些微小的水果变成梨子。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，这些特征的选择影响了继承人的坚韧。
sentences: The selection of these traits has, however, affected the heirlooms’ hardiness.
然而，这些特征的选择影响了继承人的坚韧。
They often suffer from infections that cause the fruit to crack, split, and otherwise rot quickly.
他们经常受到感染，导致水果裂开、分解，或者迅速腐烂。
Wild plants must continuously evolve to fend off such infections, points out Roger Chetelat of the Tomato Genetics Resource Center at the University of California.
加州大学番茄基因资源中心的Roger Chetelat指出：“野生植物必须不断演化，以抵御这种感染。”
But in their quest for size, shape, and flavor, humans have inadvertently eliminated defensive genes.
但是在寻找大小、形状和口味的过程中人类无意中消灭了防御基因
As a result, most possess only a single disease-resistant gene.
因此，大多数人只拥有单一的抗病基因。
Chetelat elaborates that heirlooms’ taste may have less to do with their genes than with the productivity of the plant and the growing environment.
Chetelat指出，继承人的品味与其基因有关，不如与植物的生产力和不断增长的环境有关。
Any plant that produces only two fruits, as heirlooms sometimes do, is highly likely to produce juicier, sweeter, and more flavorful fruit than varieties that produce 100, as commercial types do.
任何只生产两种水果的植物，如传承的宝藏，都极有可能生产比生产100种品种更丰富、更甜美和更有味的水果，商业类型也是如此。
In addition, heirlooms are sold ripened on the vine, a certain way to get tastier results than allowing them to mature on the shelf.
此外，继承物在葡萄树上被撕碎，这是取得美味结果的一种方法，而不是允许它们在架子上成熟。
This means breeders feel confident that getting germ-beating genes back into heirlooms won’t harm the desirable aspects of the fruit.
这表示育种者有信心，将杀菌基因带回传世宝不会损害水果的预期方面。
Modern breeding has resuscitated grocery-store tomatoes with an influx of wild genes; in the past 50 years, as many as 40 disease-resistant genes have been bred back into commercial crops.
现代育种使杂货店的西红柿恢复了活力，野生基因大量流入；在过去50年中，多达40种抗病基因被重新培育到商业作物中。

paragraphs.brief: 原始的传承宝植物Heath解释说，它有瑕疵的花朵，这就是为什么它只生产两颗水果的原因之一，而他从他的新品种中获得了30颗水果。
sentences: In 1996, a tomato breeder and former Tanksley student named Doug Heath began a favorite project.
1996年，一个番茄育种者和前Tanksley学生名叫Doug Heath 开始了一个最受欢迎的项目。
After 12 years of traditional breeding with the help of molecular markers, he created a new multi-colored tomato less prone to cracking and also endowed with 12 disease-resistant genes.
经过12年的传统育种借助分子标记，他创造了一个新的多色番茄较不易裂开，并拥有12种抗病基因。
The original heirloom plant, Heath explains, had defective flowers, which is one reason why it produced only two fruits compared with the 30 he gets from his new variety.
原始的传承宝植物Heath解释说，它有瑕疵的花朵，这就是为什么它只生产两颗水果的原因之一，而他从他的新品种中获得了30颗水果。
He claims he is also able to maintain a comparable flavor and sugar profile even on productive plants.
他声称，即使在生产工厂中，他也能保持一种可比的口味和糖的特征。
The heirloom’s defects are, after all, just an accident of a narrow breeding strategy left over from the very beginning of genetic modification.
毕竟，传承宝的缺陷只是基因改变一开始留下的狭隘育种策略的意外。

items.en: an explanation of research aimed at restoring the health of the heirloom 1tomato
items.zh: 对旨在恢复继承人健康的研究的解释
items.why: 题干抓点:“旨在恢复传家番茄 (heirloom) 的健康”。F段讲Doug Heath 通过分子标记+传统育种，把抗裂、抗病基因引回去，同时保持风味一这就是为了“把健康基因补回来” 的研究与做法，最贴合“aimed at restoring health”。

items.en: a reference to a false belief about the heirloom tomato
items.zh: 提到对传承的番茄的错误信念
items.why: 题干抓点:“对传家番茄的一个错误观念 (false belief) ”。A段先写“爱好者以为传家番茄基因更优更多样”,随后用研究直接否定，属于“错误观念”的引用与澄清。

items.en: a description of the flavor of the heirloom tomato
items.zh: 描述传承的西红柿口味
items.why: 题干抓点:“对传家番茄风味的描述”。E段明确用juicier sweeter, more flavorful, tastier描述其味道与口感。

items.en: a reference to a single gene that significantly improves the cultivation of tomatoes
items.zh: 提到一个能够显著改善西红柿种植的单一基因
items.why: D段举出一个能将果实大小提高约一半的基因，是单一基因显著改善番茄性状的实例。

items.en: The transplanting of certain genes into tomatoes can change their shape.
items.zh: 将某些基因移植到西红柿可以改变它们的形状。

items.en: The flavor of the heirloom tomato is largely dependent on actual yield and cultivation.
items.zh: 土生土长的番茄的味道主要取决于实际产量和种植量。

items.en: A new type of tomato can be produced that is stronger than the original heirloom tomato yet equally sweet and flavorsome.
items.zh: 一种新型的番茄可以生产比原始的传承型番茄更强大但同样甜美和口味。

items.en: The wide variety of heirloom tomatoes is due to only a small number of genes.
items.zh: 传承性西红柿种类繁多，其原因只是少数基因。

items.en: There is little information on the origin of the tomato despite the existence of ________ data on the growing of other New World crops.
items.zh: 关于其他新大陆作物的种植，现存的资料相当________，但人们对番茄的起源所知甚少。
items.why: 回到对应内容“但是科学家们发现了大量关于新世界早期耕作方法的考古证据，而在番茄方面，记录是空白的”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Although it is uncertain, the tomato is thought to have first grown in the ________.
items.zh: 番茄最初可能生长在________，不过这一点尚未确定。
items.why: 抓点:“被认为最早生长在”。直接对应 Andes。

items.en: In regard to genetic similarities, the type of tomato ________ is the nearest to the earliest.
items.zh: 从遗传特征来看，________这一品种与最早的番茄最为接近。
items.why: 抓点:“在基因相似性上，与最早期最近的是哪一种 '番茄类型'”。这里指currant tomato (醋栗番茄)。注: 图稿里个别版本会排成“current”,属印刷/转录小错，正确应为 currant。

items.en: A genetic ________, which is evident in pomodoro, produced larger tomatoes.
items.zh: 在名为 pomodoro 的番茄身上可以看到，一种遗传上的________使果实变大了。
items.why: 回到对应内容“1500年代来自西班牙的第一份西红柿书面记录证实，这种通过产出称为小木薯的隔间而扩大西红柿的突变，存在于给意大利人以pomodoro这个词或金苹果的同一黄西红柿中”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: ________ are a problem for heirloom tomatoes because they frequently lead to damage and deterioration.
items.zh: 对于传家宝番茄品种来说，________是个问题，因为这常导致果实受损、变质。
items.why: 抓点:“某问题导致损伤与腐坏 (damage and deterioration)”, 直接对应 infections。注意不是“diseases”,原文用词更具体为 infections。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 题干抓点:“对传家番茄风味的描述”。E段明确用juicier sweeter, more flavorful, tastier描述其味道与口感。
回到对应内容“1500年代来自西班牙的第一份西红柿书面记录证实，这种通过产出称为小木薯的隔间而扩大西红柿的突变，存在于给意大利人以pomodoro这个词或金苹果的同一黄西红柿中”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: There are probably no more than 10 mutant genes ….”
“that create the diversity of heirlooms you see”修饰前面的 genes。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 genes，再把修饰信息接回主句。
One might assume …, but that’s not the case: the Mother Tomato has never been found.
“that one of these known wild species became today’s cultivated crop”补足 assume 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 assume 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Heirloom tomatoes—varieties that have been passed down through several generations of a family because they are thought to have a particularly good flavor—are really no more “natural” than the varieties available in grocery stores.
长生不老的西红柿——由于被认为有特别好的口味而传承给一个家庭的几代人的不同品种——与杂货店的品种相比，实际上没有什么比这些品种更 " 自然 " 了。
New studies promise to restore their lost, healthy genes.
新的研究保证恢复他们丢失的、健康的基因。
